# Bounding an iteration at a declared number of rounds

The bundled `loop_counter` kind iterates a declared number of times and tags
each round as still-looping or final. The whole loop lives in the template — no
custom executor.

## The template

```yaml
name: loop-cap-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: counter
    kind: loop_counter
    subscribes:
      - node: counter
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "\"loop\" in payload.tags"
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 4}
          count: {type: integer}
```

The node subscribes to its own success, filtered on the `loop` tag. When the
final round is tagged `done` instead, the subscription stops matching and the
iteration ends.

## Drive it

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
```

## What the product does

With `max: 4` the node dispatches four times, emitting:

| count | tags |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `["loop"]` |
| 2 | `["loop"]` |
| 3 | `["loop"]` |
| 4 | `["done"]` |

Exactly one round in the sequence is marked as last, so a downstream node can
subscribe on `"done" in payload.tags` and act only on the final round.

With `max: 1` the node dispatches once, emitting count 1 tagged `["done"]`. The
degenerate case is marked too, rather than left ambiguous.

Both instances come to rest with no live runs, so the iteration stopped at the
declared bound rather than pausing.
